h1: The 5 Best Lawn Mowers for Narrow Gates of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Narrow Gate Lawn Mowers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 lawn mowers for narrow gates scored on deck width, power source and weight, from a 12 inch corded combo to a 16 inch cordless.
summary: The Litheli 14 inch cordless is the best narrow-gate mower for most backyards, since it combines a slim deck, a 5.0Ah battery and a light push frame. The MZK 13 inch is the pick when even 14 inches feels tight. The BLACK+DECKER 12 inch corded combo is the narrowest of all, and the LawnMaster and Greenworks suit gates with a little more room.
intro: The number on a mower box that matters for a narrow gate is not the one you think. Cutting width is the deck, and the machine you push through the gate is wider than that, because wheels, handle posts and the discharge chute all stick out past the blades. A 16 inch deck does not mean a 16 inch mower, and plenty of buyers find that out when the mower jams between two fence posts.

So we ranked on deck width as a proxy and built the order around it, then weighed power source and weight. We reviewed five compact electric mowers from their listings, covering 12 to 16 inch decks. No listing gives an overall width, so measure your gate's clear opening and compare it with the deck figure, leaving a margin of a few inches.

products.name: Litheli Cordless Lawn Mower 14 Inch
products.verdict: A 14 inch cordless deck with a 5.0Ah battery and charger included, on a light push frame.
products.description:
Litheli's 14 inch mower is the narrowest practical deck here with a real battery in the box: a 5.0Ah pack and charger are included. Five height positions run from 1 to 2.5 inches, covering most turf. The lightweight push design is what makes it easy to manoeuvre through a gap.

It ranks first because it removes both of the usual narrow-mower compromises, the cord and the tiny battery. Against the MZK 13 inch it adds a bigger battery and an extra inch of cut, and against the 12 inch BLACK+DECKER it needs no outlet. It costs $50 to $100.

Buy it if your yard is small and a cord would snag on beds. The caveat: 14 inches is still a deck width, so measure your gate before ordering.
products.idealFor: Small yards behind narrow gates that want a cord-free mower.
products.skipIf: Your gate is narrower than about 16 inches.

products.name: MZK 20V 13-Inch Electric Lawn Mower
products.verdict: A 13 inch brushless cordless deck on a 20V platform for side strips and very small yards.
products.description:
MZK's mower cuts 13 inches, with a brushless motor and a compact cordless design on a 20V battery platform. The brushless motor is a quiet advantage: it wastes less energy as heat, so a small battery stretches further.

It ranks second because the Litheli lists a bigger 5.0Ah battery and charger, while MZK states only a 20V platform. What it offers is one fewer inch of deck, which is the difference between squeezing through a gate and not, and it costs $100 to $200.

Choose it for side yards where even 14 inches feels tight. The caveat: with no battery capacity stated, check whether a battery is included before ordering, and expect shorter runtime on thick grass.
products.idealFor: Side strips and very small yards with tight access.
products.skipIf: You want a stated battery size included.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER Electric Lawn Mower, Weed Eater and Edger 3-in-1 Combo
products.verdict: A 12 inch corded mower that doubles as a trimmer and edger, the narrowest and cheapest option.
products.description:
This BLACK+DECKER is the narrowest tool here at a 12 inch cutting width, with a corded 6.5 amp motor. It converts into a trimmer and edger, which suits a yard with beds, borders and a gate narrow enough to need one tool for everything.

It ranks third because the cord limits reach and drags across plantings, and because a 6.5 amp motor is the lightest powered here. Against the Litheli it costs about the same, $50 to $100, but you give up the battery. What you gain is a deck 2 inches narrower and a three-job tool.

Buy it if you have a patch of lawn and one extension cord. The caveat: the 12 inch deck means many passes on anything bigger than a postage-stamp lawn.
products.idealFor: Tiny yards with a single outlet and tight gate access.
products.skipIf: Your lawn is large or far from an outlet.

products.name: LawnMaster MEB1114K Electric Corded Lawn Mower
products.verdict: A 15 inch corded mower with an 11 amp motor and no battery to replace.
products.description:
LawnMaster's MEB1114K cuts 15 inches with an 11 amp corded motor, the strongest electric motor on this list. With no battery, there is nothing to degrade or replace, and runtime is unlimited as long as the cord reaches.

It ranks fourth because 15 inches leaves less gate clearance than the Litheli or MZK, and the cord is a handling chore on a yard with beds or trees. The 11 amp motor does give it the best cutting power for tougher grass, which the 6.5 amp BLACK+DECKER cannot match, and it costs $100 to $200.

Buy it for a small, open lawn near an outlet. The caveat: a cord and a 15 inch deck together make it the hardest to route through a tight gate.
products.idealFor: Small open yards near an outlet with thicker grass.
products.skipIf: Your gate is tight or your yard has many obstacles.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 16-Inch Push Lawn Mower
products.verdict: A 16 inch cordless push mower with a 40V 4.0Ah battery and charger included.
products.description:
Greenworks fits a 16 inch deck to a 40V 4.0Ah battery with a charger in the box and a push drive. It is the widest mower in this ranking, which makes it the fastest to mow but the least suited to a tight gate.

It ranks last because deck width is the point of this guide, and 16 inches is the most likely to jam. The 40V platform is a stronger system than the 20V MZK, and the established Greenworks line is easy to find batteries for. At $200 to $500, though, it is also the most expensive.

Choose it if your gate is wider than a standard 3 foot door and you want less mowing time. The caveat: it costs far more than the Litheli for two extra inches.
products.idealFor: Homes with a wider side gate and a small lawn.
products.skipIf: Your gate is genuinely narrow or budget is tight.

whatMatters.detail: Deck width is the cutting width of the blade housing, from 12 to 16 inches here. The mower itself is wider, because wheels and handles extend past the deck. Measure your gate's clear opening and subtract a few inches of margin. A narrower deck means more passes but easier access, which is the right trade for narrow-gate yards.

Cordless mowers like the Litheli and MZK roam freely, but the battery limits runtime. Corded mowers like the LawnMaster run indefinitely, but the cord snags on beds. For narrow gates, a cord can wedge in the opening. Check the battery size in amp hours, and count cord length against your longest run.

Voltage indicates platform strength and amp hours indicate capacity. A 40V 4.0Ah pack, like the Greenworks, runs longer than a 20V pack of similar size. Check whether the battery and charger are included, since some listings sell the tool alone. The Litheli lists a 5.0Ah battery and charger.

Brushless motors run cooler and use less battery than brushed ones, which matters when the pack is small. Corded motors are rated in amps, such as the LawnMaster's 11 amp motor. A higher amp rating means more torque in thick grass. Look for brushless or an amp figure in the listing.

A light frame is easier to lift over a threshold or step at a gate. Height adjustment decides how tall your grass can be, and the Litheli offers five positions from 1 to 2.5 inches. Check the weight in the specs, and make sure the lowest setting suits your lawn.

faq.q: How narrow a gate do I need for these mowers?
faq.a: Listings give only deck width, from 12 to 16 inches, not overall width. Measure your gate and compare with the deck, adding a margin of a few inches. A 12 inch BLACK+DECKER leaves the most room.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with narrow-gate mowers?
faq.a: Assuming deck width equals machine width. Wheels and the handle make the mower wider than the cut. Hold a tape against your gate, then add a few inches for the Litheli or MZK before ordering.

faq.q: Is a corded mower worth it over cordless?
faq.a: For a tiny, open lawn, yes. The LawnMaster's 11 amp motor runs without a battery. But cords snag at gates and in beds, so the cordless Litheli is easier for most narrow-access yards.

faq.q: How do I get a mower through a tight gate?
faq.a: Fold the handle if it allows, lift the front wheels and walk the deck through at an angle. A light mower like the Litheli makes this easier. Never remove guards or covers to save space.

faq.q: How do I maintain a cordless lawn mower?
faq.a: Remove the battery before cleaning, wipe the deck underside after each mow, and store the pack indoors. The MZK and Greenworks batteries last longer if you avoid leaving them in a hot shed or fully drained.

faq.q: Can a mower this narrow cut a larger lawn?
faq.a: It can, but slowly. A 12 to 14 inch deck means many passes, and cordless runtime may end first. For larger lawns near a wide gate, the Greenworks 16 inch with a 4.0Ah battery is more practical.

finalTake: The Litheli 14 inch is the best lawn mower for most narrow gates: slim, light and cordless, with a 5.0Ah battery in the box. Choose the MZK 13 inch for tighter openings, or the BLACK+DECKER 12 inch if you want the narrowest deck and a trimmer too. Measure the gate first, because deck width is not machine width.
